utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Loukas, are you ready to continue your cross-examination of Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Nielsen into the courtroom. Ms. Loukas, have you got any idea on how much time you would approximately need for the cross-examination of Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I would have thought I'd go most of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony on last Thursday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, when we left off last Friday afternoon, Mr. Nielsen, we were dealing with the 11th Assembly Session of the 18th of March, you'll recall. And we were at -- up to that portion where Mr. Vjestica was speaking. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, in respect of Mr. Vjestica's contribution, I take it you'd agree with me he was expressing a negative view of the negotiations that had taken thus far under the auspices of the Cutilheiro Plan.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I wouldn't necessarily use the word "negative." I think I would use the word "impatient."

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Impatient. Just in respect of that, of course, I take it you'd take the view that his contribution was less than a positive view of events. If one looks at, for example -- at the beginning of his contribution -- there I think it's the second paragraph -- "I'm not pleased with this document which is supposed to serve as the next stage in the talks."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm somewhat limited in answering your question by the fact that I don't have the minutes of the session in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could they be provided to Mr. Nielsen. And, Ms. Loukas, if you could tell us again at what page approximately we are, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. On my version, it's page 37.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Which I think means it's on page 36 of Your Honours' version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Close to 37 at least.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Very close.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I please also have the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Do you have them both before you now, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have them -- I've got them both in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Have you found the reference I was referring to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the English, yes. Not in the B/C/S yet. But we can go ahead with the question certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, just in respect of that, I got to the point where I said: I take it you'd take the view that his contribution was less than a positive view of the events. If one looks at, for example, at the beginning of his contribution, it's the second paragraph: "I'm not pleased with this document which is supposed to serve as the next stage in the talks."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is not pleased with the situation as it stands as of that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And it's quite clear that he, in contrast to Mr. Krajisnik's view of the negotiations, is adopting an approach that is much less than positive in relation to the negotiations; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as I stated earlier, my general impression, recalling the 11th Session and subsequent pre-April Assembly sessions, as I note in my report, is that Mr. Vjestica was very keen to establish a Serbian police force as soon as possible. And indeed at the following session, the 12th Session on the 24th of March, Mr. Vjestica stated, as I state on page 30 of my report, that he thought there had been an understanding that a Serbian police force should be established immediately, and he was not happy that it looked as if he would have to wait a bit longer for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Nielsen, we'll come to the next session. But still dealing with the 18th of March at this point, you've got Mr. Vjestica saying things like -- and this is three paragraphs down -- "These talks are used only to lull us to sleep." Do you see that portion? "To divert our attention away from what they are doing and have already done."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that passage in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So it's quite clear, is it not, that there is quite a -- a fundamental difference of approach there in the Assembly sessions between Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Vjestica?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that in the sense that Mr. Krajisnik has stated that there -- negotiations are ongoing and in the sense that Mr. Vjestica does not seem particularly pleased by developments in these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And -- and, in fact, right at the end of Mr. Vjestica's contribution, he says: "Mr. President, I think you have to give us an order that after the next Assembly you should order this, that we arrange for areas where it has not been done and to implement this, that the Serbs would occupy their territories so that no other forces could enter them. Thank you," and he sits down to applause. Do you see that portion there?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And, again, that's in contrast to the approach that's been adopted by Mr. Krajisnik throughout his contributions to the debate on the 18th of March, where -- which were more in the lines of the negotiations proceeding well and we are hopeful, in essence; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I note that on page 45 of the English version, Mr. Krajisnik, who's presiding over the Assembly session, refers back to Mr. Vjestica's comments. And at that point in the session, he acknowledges that Mr. Vjestica is somewhat in a hurry. And, again, he discusses the course of action as he sees that it should proceed. But in -- clearly, again, as I stated, this is consistent with Mr. Vjestica's impatience and his eagerness to get the ball rolling, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, looking at that contribution that you've just referred to by Mr. Krajisnik, and that is at my page 46. That would be page 45, I think, of Your Honours' copy. As Mr. Nielsen has referred to, when you look at Mr. Krajisnik's comments there, where he's saying "one explanation that has to do with what Mr. Vjestica has said about us being in a hurry," it's -- it's quite clear at that point, is it not, that Mr. Krajisnik's actually trying to calm him down, as Mr. Vjestica is coming across as something of a hot head; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could take that interpretation. I do note that on the major points, including the urgent establishment of a Ministry of Internal Affairs for the Serbian Republic that there is no disagreement there between Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Vjestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But, of course, what Mr. Krajisnik says in regard to that context, refers to responsible government and the negotiations in the sense of the negotiators should maintain their positions, and it's quite clear there that Mr. Krajisnik is referring to the ongoing negotiations; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe he is referring to the ongoing negotiations, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, before we leave that session, there's also a reference, I think, there to Mr. Zepinic on -- well, that would be page 47 of the English version. There's a contribution by Mr. Rajko Kasagic and he's asking that certain allegations of corruption in relation to Mr. Zepinic be investigated.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Have you seen any other further documents in relation to this particular question in your research?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. And indeed Vitomir Zepinic, deputy minister of SRBiH MUP at the time, was one of at least three senior SRBiH MUP officials against whom serious allegations of corruption had been made during this period; that is to say, March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just before we leave the 18th of March session, towards the end there, again - I think it would be page 44 on the English version - where there's a response by Dr. Karadzic, and he refers to "doing whatever is necessary on the ground to establish the de facto situation based on justice and the law., to have good and complete control of our destinies and areas with full respect for citizens of other nationalities. That is what people will be judged by." Do you see that contribution there, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am looking for it. On page 44?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it on the bottom of my page 45, so it may be at the bottom of your page 44 or the top of your page 45.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, again, I think that Dr. Karadzic's contribution there is, again, in the context of the continuing negotiations and what should happen on the ground should be in accordance with law and justice; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So he says.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And indeed he refers there at one point, again, in the context of the Cutilheiro negotiations, and indicates that "There will probably be all sorts of resettlements going on but none of it should occur under pressure." Do you see that portion there?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not immediately. Perhaps you could direct me to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's on my page 46, so I'm assuming that you will have it. It's -- it's the third-last paragraph from the end of Mr. Karadzic's response there.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see it now. He states that "We see that Serbs from Livno are resettling," and so forth," which is all a natural part of such a dangerous process of an intense process of reorganising a state."

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And, again, this is all in the context of the negotiations in relation to the Cutilheiro Plan; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The negotiations were ongoing at this point. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And this entire Assembly session is, of course, related to the discussions in relation to these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just going back to the text of your report, Mr. Nielsen, and that is in relation to paragraph 74 of your report, where you refer specifically to the 18th of March, 1992 session. You have there Mr. Krajisnik, the president of the Assembly, referring specifically to the need for ethnic separation on the ground, and then you have -- your next sentence begins: "Miroslav Vjestica, an SDS delegate from Bosanska Krupa, referred to the need for the establishment of a Serbian police force and a Serbian MUP so that Serbs could seize control of their territories." Now, the -- the way that you've written your report seems to indicate there's a seamless approach there on the 18th of March, 1992 session from Mr. Krajisnik's contribution to Mr. Vjestica's contribution; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't use the term "seamless approach." I think what I'm indicating here and what is borne out by the Assembly minutes as we just saw them, is that while there may be disagreements at this particular stage about the methodology of establishing a Serbian police force, both Krajisnik and Vjestica at this session agree that a Serbian police force should be established in order to control territory that they view as Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But nevertheless, Mr. Nielsen, if someone were to read this report without going to the footnote and without going through the Assembly session, one might gain the impression that the views expressed are identical.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this particular narrow point, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So in the circumstances, Mr. Nielsen, you'd agree with me that for the text to take in the complete context, in your assessment of Mr. Krajisnik's contribution the bold reference to ethnic separation on the ground, without reference to the context of the discussion on the Cutilheiro Plan, could be quite misleading, could it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated before, my brief was not to provide a full explanation of what was going on with respect to international negotiations at that time, and in fact I do believe that quite a lot of the context for that was provided in the Bosnian Serb leadership report of Mr. Treanor to which this report basically adds with specific respect to the Ministry of Internal Affairs. My understanding in writing this report was that the Trial Chamber would have at its disposal a full report on the Bosnian Serb leadership which would include that context to which you just referred.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So you do concede it could be quite misleading taken in the way you have written it there.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If someone were to read this report and nothing else, yes, one could form the opinion that Krajisnik and Vjestica fully agreed about both methodology and the goal; whereas, my intent in paragraph 74 was to highlight the fact that they agreed on the goal of ethnic separation on the ground and on the goal of the establishment of a Serbian police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But nevertheless it's quite clear, is it not, Mr. Nielsen, that Mr. Krajisnik's contribution and Mr. Vjestica's contribution are very different in tone and content?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I find them to be different with respect to the methodology, but to be consistent with respect to their shared goal.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, methodology, of course, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas -- Ms. Loukas, I think the point you'd like to make is very clear. Of course you could go on for another 15 minutes to see whether you can get any concessions out of Mr. Nielsen. I think the point you made is -- is -- in the context that you at least interpret the events in a quite different way and you put different emphasis. You put it in a context in which the words of Mr. Krajisnik would get a different meaning. Whereas, Mr. Nielsen has explained to us that he -- for limited purposes, he has for that reason drawn the attention to the words spoken by Mr. Krajisnik. I think the matter is relatively clear. And whether finally Mr. Nielsen will say for 32 or for 52 or for 53 per cent right, is not something that would assist the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm happy to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now -- now, leaving behind the 18th of March session, let's move on to the session of the 24th of March, the 12th Session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly held on the 24th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honours should have that Assembly session before you. Perhaps if the witness might also be shown that particular Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Do you have that -- I think you have both the B/C/S and the English before you, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you refer in your report at paragraph 78 to "Earlier in the day the president of the Assembly, Momcilo Krajisnik, had strongly hinted that the establishment of a Bosnian Serb police force was imminent." Mr. Nielsen, could you just inform the Trial Chamber as to which specific reference you were alluding to there in the Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as with -- is the case with most of these Assembly sessions, they are quite long. And having not examined this particular Assembly session for quite some period of time, it would take me at least a few minutes to find that passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm happy for you to take a few minutes. It shouldn't take you too long just to identify where Mr. Krajisnik is identified as speaking, and then indicating to the Trial Chamber which specific reference you're dealing with there.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps while I'm still looking here, I can briefly note that I do see that on the agenda at the outset of the session there is the second item, the Law on Ministries, which referred specifically to the -- among others, of course, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Serbian Republic, which had been already the subject of a separate law on the 28th of February in the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. I've noted that as well, Mr. Nielsen, but I'm particularly interested in where this strong hint is from Mr. Krajisnik. Is that what you're saying the strong hint is for Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, would it be a good idea to move on to the next subject and ask the witness to review the -- this session during the next break so that he's better in a position to -- to answer your questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this was the topic I wanted to deal with at this particular point. I think that Mr. Nielsen's almost finished reviewing the document, it seems to me. Is that right, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it doesn't take too much time, we could have some more patience.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I have not been able to locate it yet, the specific passage that I had in mind, so --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, in that instance --

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can examine it in more length in the pause, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: In that case, I think we will take on board His Honour, the Presiding Judge's session that during the next break you might review that particular document and see if you can find the reference.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, still on the topic of the 24th of March Assembly session, you stated there in your report that "Miroslav Vjestica complained that formation of the police force for the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina had already been agreed for that day. He saw no reason why this had to be postponed again." And then he goes on. Now, going to Mr. Vjestica's contribution - that is, I think, at -- just underneath a discussion about "proposed decision on the establishment of the National Guard." Do you see the -- Mr. Vjestica's contribution there?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see a contribution by Mr. Vjestica on pages 19 and 20 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And what page is it on the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a contribution on pages -- on page 33 of the -- of the B/C/S, 33 and 34, which corresponds to page -- the intervention on pages 19 and 20 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that's an intervention that ends -- from Mr. Vjestica that says "Why don't you deputies say it plainly here, that we have no police in any municipality, no chiefs or commanders. We do not have anything that belongs to us here, especially you who have authority on Serbian municipalities."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see that passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And, again, Mr. Vjestica seems very unhappy; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I would note that based on other documents that I've had the opportunity to review, specifically relating to Mr. Vjestica's municipality, Bosanska Krupa - and I referred to one such document last week - Mr. Vjestica's comments here do not appear to correspond to the situation on the ground in Bosanska Krupa because as of the -- I believe it's the 22nd of March, 1992, two days before this intervention in the Assembly, the Federal Secretariat for Internal Affairs in Belgrade notes that there is a Serbian police force that exists in Bosanska Krupa municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. But of course the point that Mr. Vjestica is making apparently in his contribution is that all the rest of the Serbian municipalities have no authority but in Bosanska Krupa, we're okay, and you guys don't know what you're doing and have no authority. That's basically what his contribution is there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, that comment of his, that is the comment that he makes. However, based on the documents of RS MUP, that again would be a comment that would not be borne out - that is to say, that contemporary documents demonstrate that the situation on the ground was different in municipalities besides Krupa or Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just in relation to Mr. Vjestica's comments, it's quite clear that here again he's coming across as a -- a bit of a hot head; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that "hot head" is a colloquial term that I would not use as an analyst. Again --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I can imagine you wouldn't. I'll use another term. Perhaps we could say that Mr. Vjestica is someone who appears to have more extreme views than others who have made a contribution to the debate on the 24th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the use of the word "extreme" presupposes, in my opinion, some kind of understanding of what the average, as opposed to the extreme, view would be. I would revert again to my previous assertion that I find Mr. Vjestica to be very impatient, again with -- with respect to the specific issue that I am dealing with in my report, that is to say, the establishment of a Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after Mr. Vjestica's contribution, of course, you then have Mr. Krajisnik speaking. And it says: "Everything that Mr. Vjestica said is correct. If you remember, we said at the beginning of this session that pursuant to the Constitution, which we cannot violate. We had to elect a premier designate. If you would like us to take a break now and designate three ministers, that would not be a problem. We shall express our opinions on that. At the end of the session it must be done following some kind of order. Mrs. Plavsic has arrived. We shall take a break, hold consultations, propose a premier designate, and adopt the decision. And if he could then propose the necessary ministers, the Minister of National Defence, Ministers of the Interior and foreign affairs and Minister of Finance. As to the establishment of the National Guard, I think that anything that is introduced without having first all the necessary preparations completed is doomed to failure. There is no reason why we would not establish it, but we must bring it into line with the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can we do it the way I said, Mr. Vjestica?" All right? Now, if you look at Mr. Krajisnik's contribution there after Mr. Vjestica's contribution, it's quite clear, isn't it, that again Mr. Krajisnik is trying to calm him down and bring some order to the proceedings; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- I would not take that interpretation. In fact, it seems to me, based on Mr. Krajisnik's intervention immediately following Mr. Vjestica, that Mr. Krajisnik is to a significant degree adjusting his position and indeed adjusting the work of the Assembly to approximate the position of Mr. Vjestica; that is to say that he now states - Mr. Krajisnik, that is - that "We shall take a break and essentially do much of what Mr. Vjestica has just asked us to do. And indeed I would note that - this is the 12th Assembly Session - that they do on the same day, the 24th of March, 1992, take a break. They come back. And at the 13th Session, which is the same day, they proceed to do exactly that and appoint Mico Stanisic Minister of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just in relation to your answer, Mr. Nielsen, the appointment of the Minister of Internal Affairs is -- that is quite a different thing to what Mr. Vjestica is talking about at the end of his contribution, is it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do -- with specific respect to the police, the establishment of the Serbian police of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is something that Mr. Vjestica seeks and most certainly within the context of the Law on Internal Affairs passed by the Serbian Assembly in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the appointment of a minister was an important milestone on the road to the formal establishment and debut of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. But the appointment -- the formal appointment of a minister, that's not all Mr. Vjestica wants, is it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not all that he wants. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just, again, looking at Mr. Krajisnik's contribution there. He's basically, you'd agree with me, with Mr. Vjestica trying to calm him down by saying, "Everything you say is correct," and then sidelining the discussion by saying, you know, "Mrs. Plavsic is here, why don't we listen to her." He's trying to cut him off, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if he were trying to cut him off, then I would find it odd that -- that he then in essence yields the floor to Mr. Vjestica when he says, "Can we do it the way I said, Mr. Vjestica?"

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, that's just -- that's not unusual in terms of trying to run some sort of orderly proceeding, is it, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can only speculate here, but certainly it was within the power of the chairperson of the Assembly to have moved directly on to the next speaker had he wanted to completely sideline Mr. Vjestica rather than giving him the opportunity to speak again. And indeed we note that Mr. Vjestica uses his second opportunity to intervene here to, as it were, push the envelope once again, with respect to the assumption of power and the establishment of -- of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just in relation to your last answer, Mr. Nielsen, "Well, certainly it was within the power of the chairman of the Assembly to have moved directly on to the next speaker," but there's a polite way of sidelining someone, is there not? And that's part of the skill of a speaker of the Assembly, is it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you're asking me to speculate on polite or rude ways of sidelining speakers, I -- I do suppose there are two -- two ways of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. handling that particular situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're moving to another subject or --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I am moving on to another subject, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, going on to another reference you've made to Mr. Krajisnik in your report, and that is at paragraph 87 of your report. Now, have you got that portion of your report that I'm referring to there, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I -- I'm sorry, may I hold onto this, since I was asked to review it during the next break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is this the original version we have?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's the exhibit, Your Honour, I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'd rather have a copy provided to Mr. Nielsen so that the exhibit remains in the hands of Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Nielsen, in terms of the documentation that you've used as part of your research for your report, quite clearly the vast percentage of the material you've used, of course, is documents relating to Assembly sessions and various municipality documents and draft reports of MUP, and generally they're that sort of document; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would phrase it more specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If you could do that.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The vast majority of -- or vast percentage, as you state, of the material that I have used are documents that stem from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the RS and the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is also the case that I used to a lesser extent the materials to which you referred, including the minutes of Assembly sessions, as we've seen, and various municipality documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that's because of what the focus of -- and your terms of reference were. In essence, the internal workings of the MUP. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, in relation to paragraph 87, you're not using as your reference point there the type of document we've just been discussing, are you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I'm looking at the same paragraph 87 --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, the one that begins: "A firsthand account of the collapse of the SRBiH MUP was provided by Vitomir Zepinic."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Well, in that paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Is that your paragraph 87?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Thank you. In that paragraph, I only footnote one document, and that document is a document produced by RS MUP, so I do find that to be consistent with the general type of documentation I focussed on.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, it's actually, of course, an interview with Mr. Zepinic, of course.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not an interview with Mr. Zepinic. It is a statement given to the National Security Service of the RS MUP at the end of August 1992, when Mr. Zepinic was being detained and questioned by that service. And I might note that the document itself stems from the RS intelligence and security service, which is the -- the source of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Nielsen, and of course this statement given to the National Security Service of the RS MUP at the end of August 1992 was the result of an interview with Mr. Zepinic; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question here of whether it is an interview, to my point of view of speaking as an analyst of RS MUP, this is a standard statement of a type that results from what in B/C/S is known as an "informativni razgovor," which is the standard B/C/S police term for an interrogation conducted by a -- by the police of an individual who has information that the police deemed to be relevant to the security situation. It is most usually not -- and specifically not in this case an interview done on voluntary terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, whether you use the term "police interview" or "interrogation," we are talking about somebody to produce a statement would have to be answering questions, would they not, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, in the context of what you've included there in paragraph 87, you've indicated that this is a firsthand account of the collapse of the SRBiH MUP. And now, of course, as an analyst, you would approach the account given by a person in those circumstances with some circumspection, would you not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an analyst, I would approach such an account given by a person in those circumstances with circumspection. However, I would also take into account, as I did in this case for Vitomir Zepinic, the fact that this person was at the time of the events that he was describing holding a very senior position within the Ministry of Internal Affairs and was therefore in a position to view events through his, of course, subjective point of view that would -- were not public knowledge to others in the country at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Nevertheless, Mr. Nielsen, obviously you can't vouch for the truthfulness of the account, can you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an analyst, I again would read such an account and do my utmost to compare the events described in such an account to other documents. Those could be other statements given during interrogation. They could be RS MUP or SRBiH MUP documents. And the -- on the specific issue of the meeting with Krajisnik, as I stated, I believe, last week, this is the only --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- perspective -- with Mr. Krajisnik, yes. This is the only source that we have pertaining to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. And again, of course, when you use an account such as the account that you've used, it's very difficult to form conclusions, is it not, as an analyst on the basis of one first-hand account given in the circumstances in which it was given; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, of course, it does refer to a resignation there. Now, of course, in the context of the -- the National Assembly, be it at the Bosnia-Herzegovina level or at the Serb Republic Bosnia-Herzegovina level, it's -- and perhaps you're not in a position to answer a question about the Constitution in that regard, but it's the -- the National Assembly that can elect and dismiss high-ranking officials in compliance with the law; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The National Assembly can elect and dismiss ministers in compliance with the law. That specific type of high-ranking official, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. So in reality, the -- Zepinic's resignation would have to go to the -- in relation to his position, would have to go to the then-Bosnia-Herzegovina Minister for the Interior, which was Mr. Delimustafic; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the case that Mr. Zepinic's position as Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs of SRBiH MUP would in the first instance normally require him to resign to Minister Delimustafic and not to Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Nielsen, going on to another topic, and that's back to your report specifically in relation to your discussion on the law in relation to internal affairs. Now, if you go to paragraph 169 of your report. Have you got that section of the report before you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicate there that the 1992 law, like its 1990 antecedent provided "clear and comprehensible instructions on the use of force and firearms. Citizens including suspected criminals and their private property were accorded definite rights and privileges. And then you say: "However, the 1992 RS law systematically removed all references from the 1990 law that characterised engagement in inappropriate activities as misconduct." So we're both on the same page there?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you, of course, Mr. Nielsen, you're not a lawyer and you of course don't put yourself forward as a legal expert.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And when you referred to the 1992 law systematically removing all references from the 1990 law that characterised "engagement in inappropriate activities as misconduct," I take it you're referring to, firstly -- and now we go to paragraph 146 -- you're referring in part to this: "The 1992 law completely eliminated Article 102 of the 1990 law. That article reads as follows: "Workers of the Republican Secretariat may not engage in activities that are incompatible with their duty." Do you see that portion?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. And who were the workers of the Republican Secretariat?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this case, I would like to check the -- the B/C/S original to be absolutely sure, but generally I believe, if I've used the term "workers" here, the B/C/S term should be in the -- in Article 102 of the one -- 1990 law, it should be "radnici", workers, which is to say employees in a more general English language sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And if you could please tell the Trial Chamber who the employees of the Republican Secretariat are.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- the workers of the Republican Secretariat would include the police officers of the Ministry of Internal Affairs - excuse me - as well as all other legal employees of the Republican Secretariat. I remind the Chamber that at this stage - that is to say, in 1990 - this was earlier called the Secretariat for Internal Affairs, rather than the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Nielsen. Now, if we go on to -- further on to your discussion, further in paragraph 146, you indicate: "The deletion of this article as well as the corresponding clause in Article 120 of the 1990 law removed any sanctions against actions that would have been considered incompatible with policing in the SRBiH MUP." So you've referred there to Article 20. So when we go down to your discussion on Article 20, which is in paragraph 154 of your report.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 120.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. And that's in paragraph 154 of your report. You indicate there at the bottom of the paragraph, just before paragraph 155 starts that "As mentioned above, clause 12 of this article of the 1990 law which prohibits involvement incompatible with official duty is not present in the corresponding article of the 1992 law." So those portions that I've just indicated to you, Mr. Nielsen, I take it they're the portions that you're referring to in relation to what you say at paragraph 169: "However, the 1992 RS law systematically removed all references from the 1990 law that characterised engagement in inappropriate activities as misconduct." I take it that's what you're referring to when you make that statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, this aspect of clause 12, prohibiting involvement in activities incompatible with official duty, I take it on your reading of it that what you're talking about is action or -- that undermines the performance of duties; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the word here is "incompatible," which would suggest that there were certain activities that would not be compatible with official duty, and that is to say they would have a detrimentary effect on official duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed. So that if something was incompatible with official duty, it would undermine the performance of your duties, would it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, I know you're no lawyer, Mr. Nielsen, but if you look at clause 7 in paragraph 154, you'll see that it already includes there "any action or negligence which aggravates, thwarts, or undermines the performance of duties."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see point 7 there.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So that point, in relation to incompatible duty, is actually already covered by clause 7. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see point 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So your conclusion that "The RS law systematically removed all references from 1990 law that characterised engagement in inappropriate activities as misconduct," is rather overstating it, is it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I certainly do see your point regarding point -- number 7 of Article 120 in the 1990 law. I would note that it is indeed the case also, as we see in the operation of RS MUP and indeed in the minister, Mico Stanisic's, interview that we looked at last week, that RS MUP did in practice take actions with regard to actions that the ministry saw as aggravating, thwarting, or undermining the performance of duties. And I would specifically refer to the order given by Minister Stanisic to transfer such persons who -- who did perform in such a negligent or unsatisfactory manner to the Army of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And indeed it's an unfortunate phenomenon worldwide, is it not, Mr. Nielsen, that often individual police officers do things that are against the basic tenor of what they should be doing as police officers?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, all present-day police departments or Ministries of Internal Affairs contain internal affairs bureaus within the ministry or within the police department to investigate precisely that type of misconduct or allegations thereof.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed. Thank you, Mr. Nielsen. Now, just moving on to another topic, and that is -- I just need to find the particular document that I need. Now, going back to your report - and I'm now referring to page 11 of your report, and that is paragraph 10 - you indicate there that "In a letter sent to the council of the SDS in Sarajevo in July 1991, Goran Zecevic, a Bosnian Serb and former employee of SRBiH MUP presented a litany of grievances." Now, just in relation to that, the use of the term "a litany of grievances" appears to be somewhat disparaging language, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my use of the word "litany" here is meant to denote a series of grievances or a group of grievances that are stated quite vociferously. I am not, in using the word "litany" here, trying to give any valued negative or positive connotation to the actual grievances themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Because when one looks at the list of grievances, it's quite clear on your reading of the documents, is it not, that some of these grievances were legitimate or understandable in the context?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can state is that the grievances cited by Goran Zecevic in this letter are numerous and that they are important on a wide variety of matters regarding the operation of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. However, I am not in a position to state in any exhaustive way how legitimate or illegitimate those grievances are.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, moving along to another portion of your report. You refer at paragraph 20 to the war in Croatia and its impact on the Socialist Republic of BiH MUP and relations between Serbian and Muslim police officers in North-Western Bosnia. Now, and your -- you refer there to July 1991, Zupljanin requesting urgently that the police be fully mobilised. And, of course, that was in the context of the war that was occurring in Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And so Zupljanin asserts that "It's necessary due to the deteriorating security situation and the risk of spillover from the war in Croatia." Now, Delimustafic, of course -- Mr. Delimustafic, who you cite as "Delimustafic" in your report "refused to approve Zupljanin's repeated requests." Now, in the context of what you've seen, Mr. Nielsen, the request being made by Mr. Zupljanin there was reasonable, was it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that -- I can speculate, but I don't think I can make an assertion of what is reasonable or unreasonable with respect to that specific request.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, fair enough, Mr. Nielsen. Can you assist the Trial Chamber as to what the reasons were for the refusal by Mr. Delimustafic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case, I would like to be able to refer to the original document, if I'm going to be asked specific questions about its content.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So at this point you can't really assist with the reasons for the refusal; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can state that as a general matter, based on my study of SRBiH MUP documents and other sources, including intercepted telephone conversations from this period of the summer and fall of 1991, I think it is a fair observation to state that there was a fundamental difference of opinion between Serbs in SRBiH MUP and Muslims in SRBiH MUP with respect to the war in Croatia; whereas, the Serbs tended to see the conflict in Croatia as a war that was being undertaken to preserve the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and saw establishment of Serb autonomous districts in -- on the territory of the Socialist Republic of Croatia in that context, Muslims, and it should be stated also Croats, in MUP of SRBiH tended to take quite an opposite view, which is to say that they viewed the SAO, the Serb autonomous districts established on the territory of Croatia, as secessionist or ethnically exclusive enclaves that were detrimental to the security of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Nielsen, moving on to paragraph 24 of your report, you indicate there - and that's at page 16 - "Increasingly individuals at all levels of the ministry transferred their loyalty to specific parties and even persons." So, of course, this was occurring in relation to the Bosnian Croats, the Bosnian Serbs, and the Bosniak Muslims; correct? All three were, it seems clear, transferring their loyalty to specific parties, whether it be the SDA, the SDZ -- sorry, the SDA, the SDS, or the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that might be a suitable time, because I'm just about to move on to a new topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas, we'll adjourn until five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Ms. Loukas - and that's also the reason why we had a bit of a later start - the Chamber now received a letter from Mr. Krajisnik which seems to be a response to our invitation given last Friday to just write down a few points for talks he would like to have. I don't know whether you're aware of the content of this letter or not. Mr. Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: At this stage, no, Your Honour. We're currently in the process of translating it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, I have a very practical point. We now received two letters which you addressed directly to us. I was informed, although I have not received the formal translation, that your letter of last Friday did not contain a -- a list of subjects you'd like to discuss. From what I understand from the letter we received today, which is not yet formally translated but of which the content has been informally revealed to us by a translator who is also working on the translation, I'm wondering, would you like to have them filed, which would be the -- I think the best course to do. Because from what I understand, there are also some technical matters, how to get material from countries involved, which is a matter that would certainly also be of importance for the Prosecution to know that at least Mr. Krajisnik is struggling with it. How would you like us to deal with the letter? If you'd say, "I'd like to have it filed," then it's just -- it will be translated, it will be filed, it's there -- it's -- it's on the record. If you'd say, "Since it also pertains to my relation with my Defence counsel, I would rather have it filed but then confidential," then whatever subject would be suitable for open discussions could be discussed in this courtroom, whatever would be strictly reserved for conversations with Defence counsel, whether or not in the presence of Mr. Harhoff and the Registry, we would keep it for that. I would like to know what your position is.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just prior to that, Your Honour, if I might intervene at this point just briefly. It seems to me that it -- it may be a matter which Mr. Krajisnik may require some advice from his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: -- counsel. And in the circumstances, perhaps that -- once we've had the letter translated, that we're in a better position to hopefully helpfully advise Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the question is there. I do not ask you to answer it immediately. Please seek advice from counsel. Think it over, Mr. Krajisnik. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know why my lawyer has reacted in this way, and she's quite right. But I would like to thank you for having pointed out that I sent this letter. I was just following your instructions. The letter contains very short indications of the themes that should be discussed. I accept the advice my lawyer has given. I think it's the best advice in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- it's quite a mixture of subjects, some of a rather technical nature. But we'll wait until it is translated, and then we'll hear from the Defence, and that is accused and counsel, how to deal with it. If you, Mr. Tieger, would have any specific position in this respect, I don't know to what extent Mr. Krajisnik would allow counsel to briefly discuss the content of the matter with you, and if that would raise any issue, we would like to hear from you. Then we'll hear, if not today, then at least next Thursday, because we will not be sitting -- unless, Ms. Loukas, you will send us an informal notice in between. That could be tomorrow or day after tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you may proceed with the cross-examination of Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Nielsen, just prior to the break, we were going through specific portions of your report. And I think we just left paragraph 24. I just want to take you now to paragraph 41 of your report. And you indicate there some discussions that were occurring in the context of removing Mr. Zepinic from his post. You've got the paragraph before you that I'm referring to, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do; although, I -- I do believe we were discussing paragraph 20, rather than 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, I do think we were -- we'd just finished off with paragraph 24. I can check the transcript. Yes, it was paragraph 24 that we were discussing, Mr. Nielsen. That's page 28 of the transcript for Your Honours and the Prosecution, and that's page 28, line 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nielsen, that's the line where questions were put to you -- one question was put to you in relation to the line "increasingly individuals at all levels of the ministry transferred their loyalty to specific parties." You then asked whether that was true for SDA, SDS, and HDZ, and you confirmed that, if my memory does not -- is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for -- for confirming that. I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, moving on to paragraph 41, as I was indicating, there were some discussions occurring there in the context of removing Mr. Zepinic from his post. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. And you note in your report in the last sentence of that particular paragraph that at that point Mr. Krajisnik, as president of the Assembly, suggested that both Zepinic and Stanisic be appointed, that they both be appointed. Now, that appears, of course, to be something of a conciliatory approach on the part of Mr. Krajisnik; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Although, we should note here that this specific paragraph refers to appointments to the SDS Council of Ministers and should not be confused with the later debate surrounding whether Zepinic should hold a position in RS MUP in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Mr. Nielsen. But nevertheless, in the context of -- of this particular discussion, Mr. Krajisnik is adopting an approach there of -- a conciliatory approach of trying to incorporate both Mr. Zepinic and Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, moving on to paragraph 47. And this is the report that was produced by the SRBiH MUP, information on -- on "activities in the country and abroad directed at violent change or endangerment of the constitutionally confirmed order." Now, of course, this report identifies ethnically based organisations as the main threats to law and order in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, in relation to these ethnically based organisations, clearly it was the case, Mr. Nielsen, that there were ethnically based organisations as being the main threats to law and order. That's reference, of course, to organisations involving Serbs, involving Croats, and involving Bosniak Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report does talk about groups or formations of all three groups. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, further in relation to this report, at paragraph 50, the report indicates that "Only recent activities of Muslim extremists had occurred in reaction to the proclamation of the SAOs and to the formation of Serbian paramilitary formations." Now, just in relation to that statement in the report, of course the slant of the writer must be taken into account in assessing that particular report in that regard; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that insofar as the authorship of the reports produced by SRBiH MUP at this point is known - it often isn't - that has to be taken into -- into account.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, moving on to paragraph 55 of your report, you indicate there that "Allegations were made of Muslim involvement in the illegal arms deals." Just in relation to that particular aspect, it was, of course, the case that all three ethnic nations were at some level involved in illegal arms deals; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that during this period SRBiH MUP documents show activities described as "illegal arming" among all three ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, moving on to paragraph 59 of your report. You deal there with -- "On the 14th of February, Karadzic apparently gave the signal to SDS members to initiate the second stage of preparations anticipated in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the 19th of December, 1991 instructions." Now, of course, as an analyst and as somebody whose focus is the internal workings of the Ministry of the Interior, you use the word there "apparently" because it's not something of which you can make a hard and fast claim; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And I would note that with respect to the specific series of events described on the 14th of February, that I was informed in writing that particular passage by the more expansive discussion of the same process in the report by Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed. And -- and, of course, that's -- that's a matter on which you would defer to Mr. Treanor and his expertise; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And, of course, that's a matter on which Mr. Treanor himself was cross-examined upon in April of this year -- of last year. Sorry. I take it you're aware of that. You indicated previously that you had observed some of Mr. Treanor's evidence.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, I did observe some of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just going on to the end of paragraph 75. You've got there "Mr. Krajisnik asked the deputies to think seriously before the next Assembly session about the best candidates in their regions for a Serbian MUP." Now, just in relation to that, just going back briefly to the 18th of March for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And perhaps the document could be placed again before Mr. Nielsen. I apologise, Your Honour, I should have forewarned our usher about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, if you go to -- on my version, it's page 48. It may be page 47 in your version, that is, the English version. And I think you've also got access to the B/C/S there.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you'll note there that it's got "Hence, an analysis of the record of the current officials along with nomination of new officials stating the reasons why some can be reappointed and some cannot," and then stated underneath there is: "The proposal by the president was unanimously adopted." Then it states: "At the same time, a proposal was adopted to devote more attention to appointing new officials to having more persons nominated, and even to look for the best candidates." Now, specifically in relation to that portion, "at the same time a proposal was adopted to devote more attention to appointing new officials," the record itself does not indicate that that was specifically a proposal from Mr. Krajisnik, does it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. It appears to be a -- a general proposal in front of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And -- but nevertheless you've put in your report: "Krajisnik asked the deputies to think seriously before the next Assembly session about the best candidates in their regions for a Serbian MUP."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, what I believe was my intention was to state that the -- the chairman in his capacity as chairman has the ability to put to the deputies in the Assembly that a proposal, which can be a general proposal, not coming from him personally, should be reflected upon by the time the Assembly meets the next time; that is to say, to give them the opportunity to formulate their views so that those can be presented at the following session.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But nevertheless, of course, the way it's dealt with there in your text is actually not precise in accordance with what's contained within the written record of the Assembly session; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose one could have added a -- introductory clause there stating that Krajisnik asked the deputies to think or Krajisnik acting -- Mr. Krajisnik acting in his capacity as chairman of the Assembly asked the deputy to think seriously about the best candidates in their regions for a Serbian MUP. I do not believe that I state, nor was it my intention to state, that Mr. Krajisnik had asked the deputies to think seriously about a proposal that was exclusively his.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Nevertheless, of course, anything that comes before the Assembly has to be adopted, and that's just a matter of normal political democracy in an Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, by asking the deputies to think seriously before the next Assembly session about this particular issue, Mr. Krajisnik is acting in accordance with his role as the speaker or president of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But just looking at the exact record here. All right? You've got: "At the same time, a proposal was adopted to devoting more attention to appointing new officials, to having more persons nominated, and even to look for the best candidates." Do you see what's -- what I'm referring to there, how it's specifically stated?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: All right. So it does appear to read as though at that same time the previous proposal was adopted - that was the proposal, the previous proposal by the president - a proposal - it doesn't indicate that that is a proposal by the president - was adopted to devote more attention to appointing new officials, to having more persons nominated, and even to look for the best candidates.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the passage to which you're referring.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. So all I'm asking for, Mr. Nielsen, is an acknowledgment that the text of your report there does not completely accurately reflect what's contained in the written record.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The passage to which you refer is written in the passive voice; that is to say, the second proposal referred to, there is no agency given there. It was adopted and it is not stated explicitly who proposed it, but it was adopted. And on the narrow point that if the -- if the point of contention is that -- whether Mr. Krajisnik specifically proposed that second proposal, then it is the case that it does not state here that he specifically proposed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, you have successfully drawn the attention of the Chamber to the --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- difference in text.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now -- and of course, Mr. Nielsen, in and of itself there's nothing wrong with people being asked to think seriously about best candidates for positions, is there?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of the establishment of new ministries, one would expect that serious thought would have to be given about the best candidates for positions in those ministries, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, just going on to paragraph 77 of your report. You note there that at the end of his comments, Mr. Karadzic made one final but crucial point: "The police must be under the control of the civilian authority. It must obey it. There is no discussion about that. That is the way it must be." Now, just in relation to that point, that's a fairly correct and obvious point, is it not, that the police are not a law unto themselves and any police department anywhere in the world is ultimately responsible to the relevant minister and that is a fairly uncontroversial proposition, is it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in -- it is. In this case, I think it's instructive to maybe explain a little bit more the context of this comment, and perhaps I should have done so here. What the opposite of "civilian authority" here would be -- in this specific context is military authority. So what -- the way I read Mr. Karadzic's comments at the 12th Session is that he is saying that the police must be under the control of the civilian authority, rather than military authority. This is, in fact, a demand on the part of Mr. Karadzic that can be contextualised in a situation in which the military authority in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time was held by the Yugoslav People's Army, the JNA. The Assembly, or more correctly speaking, many speakers in the Assembly and on occasion Mr. Karadzic himself, did state in previous Assembly sessions that they were not sure how the JNA was going to align itself in the context of the events as they were evolving in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They were therefore keen to make sure that the JNA would not immediately have direct control over the police. Rather, here -- as in this case here, Mr. Karadzic emphasises the need for the police to be under the control of the civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just going on to the very next paragraph, Mr. Nielsen. That was something we were dealing with earlier today, and I think you had the opportunity to take the relevant document away during the break. And I was just asking you for the specific reference there in relation to the strong hint.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for giving me an opportunity to return to that. I did have the chance to review the minutes of the 12th Session again during the break, and at this point I wish to state that based on a closer reading of it during the break, I believe that I have erred in paragraph 78 by referring to "a strong hint from Momcilo Krajisnik." The strong hint to which I referred was made by Radovan Karadzic and not by Momcilo Krajisnik. It is the case that at the 12th Session of the Assembly there is a discussion that is then brought to fruition with decisions in the 13th Session of the Assembly to move ahead with the formation of a Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs and to appoint, as it is done at the 13th Session, Mico Stanisic as the minister of that ministry. And there is no dissent from the general point, which is that all in the Assembly agree that this needs to take place. As I've stated earlier, there is some disagreement about the speed with which that needs to take place. So, again, upon having reviewed it, I believe this is a comment made by Radovan Karadzic, and I thank you for the opportunity to correct that mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nielsen. Now, just going on to paragraph 185 of your report. Now, just in the -- the context of this particular aspect, I think you've already conceded that you're not an expert on the internal workings of the SDS party. That was at -- for the benefit of the Court, page 22 of the 2nd of June transcript. Correct? You weren't -- you don't put yourself forward as an expert on the internal workings of the SDS party.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And -- nor do you put yourself forward as an expert on the functioning of the Presidency. That's page 81 of the 2nd of June transcript. Again, you don't put yourself forward as an expert on the function of the Presidency and linkages thereof; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And -- nor do you put yourself forward as an expert on Crisis Staffs. That's page 22 of the transcript, 3rd of June.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you make this statement in paragraph 185: "Until the establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska, VRS, on the 12th of May, 1992, the armed forces within RS MUP were the only armed forces exclusively and directly controlled by the RS leadership." Now, in relation to that statement, clearly, as someone who does not put themselves forward as an expert on the RS leadership, that is something that goes beyond your expertise and your terms of reference; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Ms. Loukas speak into the microphone, please, for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, if you'd put on your earphone, then you'd hear the request by the interpreters to speak in the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the degree that there is evidence brought forward by -- whether in Mr. Treanor's report or, for that matter, Mr. Brown's -- Mr. Brown's report on the functioning of the military, I would certainly defer to them on this point. In making this particular -- or in writing this particular sentence, what I'm referring to are claims made by the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs in which they were very keen in their reports, both their quarterly reports and subsequently in their draft annual report, to highlight the role of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and in particular its armed police component, to which I have previously referred, as the vanguard of the Armed Forces of the Republika Srpska. They wished to contrast the period from the beginning of April to the 12th of May, 1992, when the VRS was formally established, with the subsequent period. Again, in the context to which I referred just a few moments ago - that is to say, that the Bosnian Serb leadership and indeed senior Serbs in RS MUP displayed doubts, distrust, and other open questions about the TOs and about certain generals in the JNA - they regarded RS MUP as a fighting force, an armed force, that could be relied upon consistently during the period from the beginning of April until the 12th of May to implement the decisions that needed to be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Nielsen, moving along to paragraph 186 of your report, and I'm referring here specifically to your footnote 188, where you referred to "Zupljanin contended in his letter of the 3rd of April, 1992 that everyone had the possibility to stay in their positions." Now, just in relation to that particular document, that's a document in which Mr. Zupljanin refers to -- and it's dated 3rd of April, 1992 -- Mr. Zupljanin refers to this aspect: "In line with the Sarajevo agreement on the possible future of the state organisation of BH, the provisions of which were also confirmed in the last Brussels agreement, the collegium made a realistic appraisal of the security situation and took the view that the transformation of the existing Security Services Centre was being approached calmly and without excesses." Do you recall that particular document, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. And I would point out immediately that Mr. Zupljanin's language in that document dated 3rd April of 1992 closely paraphrases the language used in the 31 March 1992 dispatch of Momcilo Mandic, to which I referred last week as the document marking the birth of RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. And also in relation to this particular document, he refers to the fact that "It was concluded that there was no mono-ethnic aspect to the transformation of the Security Services Centre that had been carried out and that we would not permit facilities and equipment to be taken over on a mono-ethnic basis." You recall that portion of the document as well?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in relation to those two aspects, the reference to the Cutilheiro Plan or the Sarajevo agreement and the reference to not allowing facilities and equipment to be taken over on a mono-ethnic basis. You, of course, don't go to those specific aspects in your coverage of the document in footnote 188, do you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In footnote 188, I state that "He" - that is to say, Stojan Zupljanin - "contended that everyone had the possibility to state in their -- stay in their positions."

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, going on to paragraph 191 of your report, you make this claim here, in the second sentence: "The campaign to find 'illegal weapons' and remove them from the possession of the non-Serbian population evolved into the harassment, detention, and eventually expulsion of large portions of that population from the RS. This policy was formulated by the central Bosnian leadership for implementation by the police and military." Now, you, of course, firstly don't have any sort of footnote there to that particular proposition; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I do have is the following sentence, where I refer to the first such instance, which is the order from Bogdan Subotic, the RS minister of national defence on the 16th of April declaring that a state of imminent war existed and to form mobilisation. He also allowed the authorities to take "all necessary measures appropriate to the situation." It is my contention, based on having examined RS MUP documents and a smaller quantity of VRS documents, that that particular order subsequently, as I show in the report, evolves into the aforementioned disarming campaign, which leads to large-scale detentions and eventually expulsions.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, Mr. Nielsen, but nevertheless, again, as somebody who is not an expert on the internal workings of the SDS party nor an expert on the functioning of the Presidency nor an expert on Crisis Staffs, that particular conclusion is beyond the purview of your report, your terms of reference, and your expertise, is it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
